proofs.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 n=|V|+|E^{\mathrm{det}}|+|E^{?}|,
 \qquad m=|E^{?}|,
 \qquad M=|\mathfrak C|.
\]
For \(c=(F_0,F_1,A_c,K_c)\in\mathfrak C\) and \(H\subseteq E^{?}\), define the core-feasibility predicate
\[
 \Phi_c(H)=1
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \left\{
 \begin{array}{l}
 K_c\subseteq H,\quad\text{and}\\[2mm]
 \text{every }a\in A_c\text{ reaches a vertex of }Y\text{ in the directed part of}
 (V,E^{\mathrm{det}}\cup H)[V\setminus X].
 \end{array}
 \right.
 \tag{1}
\]
This is well typed because \(A_c\subseteq F_0\) and \(F_0\cap X=\varnothing\) by Definition~\ref{def:sparse-core-family}.  Reachability is monotone under edge addition, so
\[
 H\subseteq H'\ \text{ and }\ \Phi_c(H)=1
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \Phi_c(H')=1.
 \tag{2}
\]
Theorem~\ref{thm:sparse-core-reduction} identifies \(\mathcal O_{XY}\) with the globally inclusion-minimal members of
\[
 \mathscr U=\{H\subseteq E^{?}:\Phi_c(H)=1\text{ for some }c\in\mathfrak C\}.
\]
By monotonicity (2), one-edge deletions characterize global minimality:
\[
 H\in\mathcal O_{XY}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \left[
 \begin{array}{l}
 \Phi_c(H)=1\text{ for some }c\in\mathfrak C,\quad\text{and}\\
 \Phi_d(H\setminus\{e\})=0
 \text{ for every }e\in H\text{ and every }d\in\mathfrak C.
 \end{array}
 \right]
 \tag{3}
\]
Indeed, the right side says precisely that \(H\in\mathscr U\) and no one-edge deletion is in \(\mathscr U\).  If a proper subset \(H'\subsetneq H\) were in \(\mathscr U\), then for any \(e\in H\setminus H'\), (2) would put \(H\setminus\{e\}\) in \(\mathscr U\), a contradiction.  The converse is immediate.

We next construct the promised projection for one fixed core \(c\).  Add a new sink \(t\).  Let \(D_c^0\) contain the directed edges of \(E^{\mathrm{det}}\) with endpoints in \(V\setminus X\), the directed edges of \(K_c\) with endpoints in \(V\setminus X\), and a new deterministic edge \(y\to t\) for every \(y\in Y\).  Let
\[
 U_c=\{e\in E^{?}\setminus K_c:e\text{ is directed and both endpoints of }e
 \text{ lie in }V\setminus X\}.
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:edge-partition} makes the deterministic edges and the optional edges in \(U_c\) disjoint.  For each \(e\in U_c\), introduce two private vertices \(u_e^-\) and \(u_e^+\) and the private gadget edge
\[
 g_e:u_e^-\longrightarrow u_e^+.
\]
For each \(a\in A_c\), introduce a terminal copy \(\bar a\).  Form a forward transition graph by adding
\[
 \begin{array}{ll}
 \bar a\to t &\text{if }a\leadsto t\text{ in }D_c^0,\\
 \bar a\to u_e^- &\text{if }a\leadsto \operatorname{tail}(e)\text{ in }D_c^0,\\
 u_e^+\to t &\text{if }\operatorname{head}(e)\leadsto t\text{ in }D_c^0,\\
 u_e^+\to u_f^- &\text{if }\operatorname{head}(e)\leadsto \operatorname{tail}(f)
                    \text{ in }D_c^0,
 \end{array}
 \tag{4}
\]
for all well-typed \(a,e,f\), together with every gadget edge \(g_e\).  Zero-length deterministic paths are allowed in the reachability tests.  Reverse all the edges in this transition graph and call the result \(\Gamma_c\).  Its root is \(t\), its terminal set is \(\bar A_c=\{\bar a:a\in A_c\}\), and the reversed copy of \(g_e\), still denoted \(g_e\), has the unique label \(e\).  The private split vertices make the label map injective: distinct elements of \(U_c\) label distinct gadget edges, and no transition edge has a label.

For \(H\supseteq K_c\), let \(\Gamma_c[H]\) retain every unlabelled edge of \(\Gamma_c\) and retain \(g_e\) exactly when \(e\in H\cap U_c\).  Segmenting a directed path at its optional uncertain edges proves
\[
 \Phi_c(H)=1
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \Gamma_c[H]\text{ contains a directed }t\text{-to-}\bar a\text{ path for every }
 \bar a\in\bar A_c.
 \tag{5}
\]
For the forward implication, take an \(a\)-to-\(Y\) path from (1), append the corresponding \(y\to t\), and list its edges in \(U_c\) as \(e_1,\ldots,e_q\) in path order.  Each segment before \(e_1\), between \(e_i\) and \(e_{i+1}\), and after \(e_q\) lies in \(D_c^0\), so (4) gives a forward \(\bar a\)-to-\(t\) path using exactly the listed gadget edges.  Reversal gives the required path in \(\Gamma_c[H]\).  If \(q=0\), the edge \(\bar a\to t\) in (4) gives the path.  Conversely, reverse a \(t\)-to-\(\bar a\) path in \(\Gamma_c[H]\), replace every transition edge by a witnessing path in \(D_c^0\), and replace every gadget edge \(g_e\) by the original edge \(e\).  Concatenation gives an \(a\)-to-\(Y\) directed walk using only \(E^{\mathrm{det}}\cup H\) outside \(X\); deleting closed subwalks yields a directed path.  This proves (5).

The graph \(\Gamma_c\) has \(O(m+b)\) vertices and \(O(m^2+bm)\) edges.  All conditions in (4) are computable by polynomially many graph-reachability searches.  Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:directed-steiner-enumeration} to \(\Gamma_c\), root \(t\), and terminals \(\bar A_c\).  It enumerates without repetition every inclusion-minimal edge subgraph \(T\) containing a \(t\)-to-\(\bar a\) path for all \(\bar a\in\bar A_c\), with polynomial per-core preprocessing, delay, and space.  Associate to a raw subgraph \(T\) the uncertain support
\[
 L_c(T)=K_c\cup\{e\in U_c:g_e\in T\}.
 \tag{6}
\]
Equation (5) gives \(\Phi_c(L_c(T))=1\).

Different minimal Steiner subgraphs can have the same label set, so we suppress that within-core multiplicity canonically rather than storing previous supports.  Given a feasible \(H\supseteq K_c\), choose, in the fixed encoding order, one \(t\)-to-\(\bar a\) path in \(\Gamma_c[H]\) for every \(\bar a\in\bar A_c\), take their edge union, and scan that union's edges in reverse encoding order.  Delete a scanned edge exactly when all terminals remain reachable from \(t\).  Denote the final subgraph by \(C_c(H)\).  Every operation is a reachability test, so \(C_c(H)\) is computable in polynomial time.  It is inclusion-minimal: when an edge is retained, its deletion destroys a required reachability at that stage; subsequent deletions cannot restore reachability.  Therefore \(C_c(H)\) is one of the subgraphs enumerated by Lemma~\ref{lem:directed-steiner-enumeration}.  For a raw \(T\), retain it only if
\[
 T=C_c(L_c(T)).
 \tag{7}
\]
For a fixed pair \((c,H)\), at most one raw subgraph passes (7), and if \(C_c(H)\) uses every gadget labelled by \(H\setminus K_c\), exactly one passes.

We can now state the complete filter.  For each retained raw \(T\), set \(H=L_c(T)\).  Test (3) by scanning every \(e\in H\) and every \(d\in\mathfrak C\).  A test of \(\Phi_d(H\setminus\{e\})\) first checks \(K_d\subseteq H\setminus\{e\}\) and then performs at most \(|A_d|\le b\) directed-reachability searches in the graph in (1).  Reject \(H\) if any such test is positive.  Otherwise let
\[
 \operatorname{own}(H)=\min\{d\in\mathfrak C:\Phi_d(H)=1\}
 \tag{8}
\]
in the fixed core order, and output \(H\) only from the run for \(c=\operatorname{own}(H)\).  The set in (8) is nonempty because the raw subgraph itself establishes \(\Phi_c(H)=1\).

Soundness is immediate from (3): every output lies in \(\mathcal O_{XY}\), hence is globally minimal across all cores.  For coverage, fix \(H\in\mathcal O_{XY}\) and put \(c_* =\operatorname{own}(H)\).  First observe that
\[
 H\setminus K_{c_*}\subseteq U_{c_*}.
 \tag{9}
\]
Indeed, an edge in \(H\setminus(K_{c_*}\cup U_{c_*})\) is either bidirected or is a directed edge unavailable in the induced directed graph on \(V\setminus X\).  Deleting it leaves \(K_{c_*}\) present and leaves every path certifying \(\Phi_{c_*}(H)=1\) unchanged, contrary to (3).  Equation (5) makes \(\Gamma_{c_*}[H]\) feasible, so \(C_{c_*}(H)\) exists.  It must use every gadget \(g_e\) with \(e\in H\setminus K_{c_*}\).  Otherwise its paths, expanded as in the converse proof of (5), would prove
\[
 \Phi_{c_*}(H\setminus\{e\})=1,
\]
contradicting (3).  Hence (6) gives \(L_{c_*}(C_{c_*}(H))=H\).  The directed-Steiner enumerator eventually visits this canonical subgraph; it passes (7), (3), and (8), and therefore outputs \(H\).  Equation (7) prevents a second output from the same core, while (8) prevents an output from any other core.  Thus every obstruction is output exactly once.  Finiteness of \(\mathfrak C\) and exhaustion of each directed-Steiner enumerator prove termination and certified exhaustion.

For every accepted \(H\), Definition~\ref{def:obstruction-hypergraph} gives \(\operatorname{Fail}(H)=1\).  Run the fixed deterministic \(\operatorname{ID}\) procedure on that realization and record its ordered recursion trace.  Lemma~\ref{lem:ordinary-id-polynomial-decision} bounds the decision time polynomially; recording the already computed, deterministically tie-broken trace adds at most linear overhead in that computation.  This supplies the canonical original-query failure label.

It remains to account for time and space.  The proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:sparse-core-reduction} gives
\[
 M\le |V|2^{O(b\log(b+1))}.
 \tag{10}
\]
The tuple encodings in Definition~\ref{def:sparse-core-family} can be generated in their fixed order and checked in polynomial time, so (10), construction (4), and the cited per-core preprocessing bound cost \(2^{O(b\log(b+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n)\) in total over all cores.  Let \(W\) be the number of raw Steiner subgraphs examined over all core runs, with witnesses and cores counted separately.  The raw enumerators use \(\operatorname{poly}(n)\) work per raw subgraph and polynomial work before their first and after their last subgraphs.  Tests (7)--(8) and (3) use at most \((m+1)M\) core-feasibility tests per raw subgraph.  Consequently the complete exact run takes
\[
 2^{O(b\log(b+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n)(1+W)
\tag{11}
\]
time.  Process one core at a time and regenerate the core iterator on demand during (3) and (8).  One directed-Steiner state, one support bit vector, and one core-feasibility workspace then use \(\operatorname{poly}(n)\) memory; neither prior raw candidates nor prior outputs are stored.

Finally, (11) is deliberately not an accepted-output delay bound.  The filter can reject raw candidates strictly containing an obstruction feasible for a competing core, and the sparse-core reduction supplies no bound on how many such candidates can occur between two accepted outputs.  More structurally, if already certified obstructions are \(B_1,\ldots,B_q\), then a prospective support \(H\) avoids their domination exactly when
\[
 B_i\nsubseteq H\text{ for every }i
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 (E^{?}\setminus H)\cap B_i\ne\varnothing\text{ for every }i.
\tag{12}
\]
Thus partial pruning must enforce a hypergraph-transversal constraint on the excluded edges while simultaneously satisfying the existential core choice and all root-reachability groups in (1).  Proposition~\ref{prop:width-parameter-separation} shows that bounded \(b\), even \(b=2\), does not bound the incidence treewidth of \(\mathcal O_{XY}\).  Hence neither a bounded-incidence-width extension oracle nor a general-\(b\) delay bound follows from the frozen assumptions, and an explicit-hypergraph dualization bound cannot be substituted for the missing implicit coupled-extension oracle.  This proves exactly the candidate-sensitive claim.

added_lemmas.statement: For a finite directed graph with \(n_D\) vertices and \(m_D\) edges, a root \(r\), and terminals \(W_D\) not containing \(r\), all inclusion-minimal subgraphs containing a directed \(r\)-to-\(w\) path for every \(w\in W_D\) can be enumerated with \(O(n_D+m_D)\) worst-case delay after \(O(n_Dm_D)\) preprocessing and with \(O(n_D^2)\) working space.

added_lemmas.gap: The published theorem does not treat fixed deterministic edges, uncertain-edge support projection, or global domination across causal cores; those adaptations are proved in Theorem~\ref{thm:canonical-enumeration}.

proposed.justification: This is the strongest unconditional general-width compiler: it is exact and auditable, with fixed-parameter polynomial work charged to each raw projected witness.
proposed.gap: Worst-case delay between accepted obstructions remains open because deterministic support canonicalization and cross-core domination are not integrated into a bounded-time partial-extension oracle.
proposed.consumer: The uncertain-ADMG sampler and edgeID workflow can compile every minimal jointly harmful edge set offline, while the width-two theorem supplies the online polynomial-delay regime.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Remove the unresolved OEQ as a theorem premise, add the published raw directed-Steiner enumerator and the established width-separation premise, and synchronize the theorem metadata with the narrowed candidate-sensitive claim.

prose_updates.tldr: A probabilistic ADMG currently yields one high-plausibility identifiable realization, not the total chance that a fixed causal query is identifiable or the minimal edge combinations that destroy it.  The project makes those combinations the hyperedges of \(\mathcal O_{XY}\) and compresses every hedge into a \(2b-2\)-edge core plus directed ancestry obligations.  For general \(b\), the proved exact compiler projects deterministic reachability, enumerates raw minimal directed-Steiner witnesses, tests global minimality across every core, and suppresses duplicates canonically; its \(2^{O(b\log(b+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n)(1+W)\) total-time guarantee is explicitly sensitive to the number \(W\) of raw witnesses and is not an accepted-output delay bound.  The enumeration headline is the complete \(b\le2\) labelled transition-DAG and induced-path algorithm with polynomial preprocessing, worst-case delay, exhaustion, and space.  Once \(\mathcal O_{XY}\) is explicit, standard exact literal-weighted CNF model counting on a supplied incidence decomposition yields reliability and all edge sensitivities, while exact successful-realization counting is \(\#\mathrm P\)-complete already at \(b=2\).

project_justification.gap: Ordinary ID certifies failure in one ADMG by a hedge, and edgeID chooses one plausible identifiable subgraph, but neither theory compiles all globally minimal uncertain-edge causes of failure.  The additional general-\(b\) output-delay question remains open because raw candidates from one sparse core can be dominated by an obstruction from another core.
project_justification.niche: Maximum envelope district size \(b\) bounds the local bidirected and forest part of every hedge without bounding its directed ancestry paths or the incidence treewidth of the resulting obstruction hypergraph.  This separates an unconditional candidate-sensitive exact compiler from the stronger partial-extension oracle needed for accepted-output delay.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies the sparse-core representation, an unconditional exact general-\(b\) compiler with fixed-parameter polynomial work per raw projected Steiner witness and canonical global filtering, a complete polynomial-delay construction for every \(b\le2\) envelope, the reliability and sensitivity implementation corollaries, and a width-two causal counting-hardness boundary.  It retains general-\(b\) worst-case delay as an explicit open frontier.

prose_updates.related_work: Shpitser and Pearl (2008) establish soundness and completeness of ordinary ID through hedge certificates; Shpitser (2023, Proposition 1, \(\mathrm{arXiv}:2307.03750\)) gives the corrected equivalence between ID failure and a hedge for the original query.  These results supply the causal equivalence used here, not support enumeration.  Akbari et al. (2023) formulate probabilistic ADMGs and prove edge ID is NP-complete, while Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2025, Definition 6, Algorithm 2, and Lemma 7) use only the vertex-minimal hedges needed for a minimum hitting-set intervention problem in one fixed graph.  Neither work enumerates uncertain-edge-minimal failure supports across all realizations.  Kobayashi, Kurita, and Wasa (2022, Theorem 16) prove linear-delay, polynomial-space enumeration of minimal directed Steiner subgraphs.  Here that theorem is used only for raw witnesses after an injectively labelled deterministic-reachability projection; the local proof supplies support canonicalization, all-core deletion tests, and least-core ownership.  Those filters give candidate-sensitive total time, not general-\(b\) accepted-output delay.  Kenig and Mizrahi (2025) give fixed-parameter delay for minimal transversals when an explicit bounded-incidence-treewidth decomposition is supplied, but bounded causal district size does not bound the incidence treewidth of \(\mathcal O_{XY}\).  Generic explicit-hypergraph dualization likewise does not provide the missing implicit extension oracle coupled to existential core choice and multiple-root reachability, so no quasi-polynomial or fixed-parameter delay conclusion is imported from it.  Samer and Szeider (2010) and Dudek, Phan, and Vardi (2020) provide the standard exact weighted-CNF machinery used after compilation; Goharshady and Mohammadi (2020) place that computation within established reliability methodology.  Provan (1986) and Provan and Ball (1983) supply the counting-hardness sources for the width-preserving causal reduction.
prose_updates.interpretation: For envelopes with \(b\le2\), minimal failure supports can be streamed with certified polynomial delay and exhaustion.  For larger districts, the unconditional algorithm is an exact offline compiler whose runtime should be reported together with the number of raw projected Steiner witnesses and the number rejected by global domination.  Reliability and derivative computation apply after the obstruction hypergraph has been compiled; they do not convert the candidate-sensitive general compiler into a delay algorithm.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: For already accepted obstructions \(B_1,\ldots,B_q\), a prospective support \(H\) avoids domination exactly when \(B_i\nsubseteq H\) for every \(i\), equivalently when the excluded set \(E^{?}\setminus H\) intersects every \(B_i\).  Partial pruning therefore contains a hypergraph-transversal constraint coupled to an existential sparse-core choice and multiple-root reachability groups.  Bounded district size \(b\) does not imply bounded incidence treewidth for this obstruction family, so the supplied assumptions do not furnish the required extension oracle; explicit-hypergraph dualization does not justify a quasi-polynomial delay claim for the implicit coupled problem.  The proved general algorithm instead enumerates raw projected directed-Steiner witnesses, canonicalizes equal supports, and filters strict cross-core domination, which permits an unbounded number of rejected candidates between accepted outputs.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The sparse-core reduction, the candidate-sensitive exact general-\(b\) compiler, the complete \(b\le2\) labelled-transition-DAG algorithm, and the width-two counting reduction are proved results.  The general compiler has total time \(2^{O(b\log(b+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n)(1+W)\), where \(W\) counts raw projected minimal directed-Steiner subgraphs with their cores and witnesses; it makes no worst-case accepted-output-delay claim.  General-\(b\) delay remains precisely the open root-ordered partial-support recursion and coupled extension test posed by the existing OEQ.  The reliability identity, full-gradient formula, and incidence-treewidth evaluation are implementation propositions from standard exact literal-weighted CNF methods after \(\mathcal O_{XY}\) is explicit.  No claim is made that edge probabilities are calibrated, that one identifying formula is common to all successful realizations, that \(b\) controls output size or incidence treewidth, or that the candidate-sensitive compiler has been implemented.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem gives the strongest unconditional general-width result: exact global obstruction compilation with canonical duplicate suppression and fixed-parameter polynomial work per raw projected witness.
statement_notes.gap: A worst-case delay bound between accepted outputs still requires the open partial-support extension oracle that couples cross-core non-domination to multiple-root reachability.
statement_notes.consumer: The uncertain-ADMG sampler and edgeID workflow can use this as an exact offline compiler and report its raw-candidate count; online polynomial-delay reporting is certified by the width-two theorem.
